# Events

A notification says that something happened. A rule listens with `on`, binds the event's subjects by name, reads its fields as `event.field` and may `filter` on them (05 §8, §9). Every event also binds `actor` and `instigator` from its cause where the cause names them. Events mods define are listed in their own files. [Hooks](hooks.md) are on a page of their own.

<a id="ability-active"></a>
## `ability_active`

A dormant ability's `while` holds again: it confers what it lists. Its modes do not come back by themselves.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.

<a id="ability-dormant"></a>
## `ability_dormant`

An ability's `while` stopped holding (08 §6.1): it confers nothing, and its modes have ended.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.

<a id="ability-granted"></a>
## `ability_granted`

An entity came to hold an ability (08 §3.3): its first source gave it, or a rule granted again one that was revoked. What it confers is applied before this is raised.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `source` (string): What gave it: `template`, `trait` or `rule`.
- `rank` (int): Its rank now.

<a id="ability-refused"></a>
## `ability_refused`

A use of an ability was refused after `ability_using` ran, or when a rule asked for it (`use_ability`). Nothing was spent.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action.
- `reason` (string): The code of the reason.
- `message` (string): The reason, in words.

<a id="ability-restored"></a>
## `ability_restored`

The last suppression of an ability lifted: it confers again, unless it is dormant. Its modes do not come back by themselves.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.

<a id="ability-revoked"></a>
## `ability_revoked`

An entity no longer holds an ability (08 §6.3). Its modes have ended and what it conferred has been taken back.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `how` (string): `revoked` by `revoke_ability`, `lost` with its last source, or `moved` with a mind to another body (08 §3.4).

<a id="ability-suppressed"></a>
## `ability_suppressed`

Something outside an ability suppressed it (08 §6.2): it confers nothing, its modes have ended (`how` `suppressed`) and what was bound to end then has ended.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `by` (string): What suppressed it: `effect` (`suppress_abilities`), `trait` or `area`.

<a id="ability-used"></a>
## `ability_used`

A granted action was started through its ability (08 §5): the cost has been taken and the cooldown started.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action.
- `cost` (any): What was spent: a map of each pool's or item's qualified id to the amount, overdraw included.

<a id="action-abandoned"></a>
## `action_abandoned`

An action ended because its actor left the world or was removed (03 §9): `on_abandon` has run.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `id` (int): The number of the running action, which no other action of this simulation ever has.

<a id="action-cancelled"></a>
## `action_cancelled`

The actor abandoned an action in a phase that allows it: `on_cancel` has run and its channels are free.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `id` (int): The number of the running action, which no other action of this simulation ever has.
- `phase` (string): The id of the phase.

<a id="action-finished"></a>
## `action_finished`

An action ran to its end: `on_finish` has run and its channels are free.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `id` (int): The number of the running action, which no other action of this simulation ever has.

<a id="action-interrupted"></a>
## `action_interrupted`

An action was ended against the actor's will, by the `interrupt` effect, a lost channel slot, a failed `requires_at_start` or the transition limit: `on_interrupt` has run.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `id` (int): The number of the running action, which no other action of this simulation ever has.
- `phase` (string): The id of the phase.
- `code` (string): The stable code of the reason.
- `message` (string): The reason, in a sentence.

<a id="action-refused"></a>
## `action_refused`

An action that an effect or a plan asked for did not start: a failed `requires`, slots lacking, a veto. A command refused before any handler ran is told its reason directly and raises nothing; one that a handler of `action_starting` refused raises it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `code` (string): The stable code of the reason.
- `message` (string): The reason, in a sentence.

<a id="action-started"></a>
## `action_started`

An action began: its channels are claimed and its `on_start` is about to run (03 §6.6).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `id` (int): The number of the running action, which no other action of this simulation ever has.

<a id="agent-loaded"></a>
## `agent_loaded`

An agent came back into the world (09 §10.4): where its routine puts it, or on its way between two places.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `doing` (string): What its routine has it doing as it comes back.

<a id="agent-stored"></a>
## `agent_stored`

A notable resident's individual left the world with its tract and is now an agent (09 §10.4): stored, placed by its routine, costing nothing between wake-ups.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `doing` (string): What it is doing as an agent: its routine's `doing` now, or `waiting`.
- `aim` (string?): The qualified id of the goal it was pursuing, if not its routine's (09 §10.4).

<a id="area-breached"></a>
## `area_breached`

An enclosed area no longer closes; `here` is a cell it leaks through.

Subjects, in delivery order: `area` (area), `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="area-closed"></a>
## `area_closed`

A breached area closes again.

Subjects, in delivery order: `area` (area), `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="area-entered"></a>
## `area_entered`

An entity came to be inside an area. Its wake-ups have moved to the clock that now applies.

Subjects, in delivery order: `area` (area), `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="area-exited"></a>
## `area_exited`

An entity stopped being inside an area.

Subjects, in delivery order: `area` (area), `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="attr-changed"></a>
## `attr_changed`

An attribute's value changed: its base, a modifier, or something its base reads.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `attr` (id<attribute>): The attribute whose value changed.
- `old` (real): Its value before.
- `new` (real): Its value now.

<a id="became-anonymous"></a>
## `became_anonymous`

A notable individual was made anonymous again by `make_anonymous` (06 §12.2): it will be forgotten when its tract unloads.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="became-notable"></a>
## `became_notable`

An anonymous individual became notable: something about it would be lost by forgetting it (06 §12.2).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="binding-created"></a>
## `binding_created`

Something was bound to an ability (08 §7.3): a trait, a summoned entity, conjured cells, an area or a rule.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `name` (string): The name it was given (`as`), or empty.
- `what` (string): What is bound: `trait`, `entity`, `edit` (conjured cells), `area` or `rule`.
- `on_end` (string): What will happen to it when it ends: `remove`, `restore` or `release`.

<a id="binding-ended"></a>
## `binding_ended`

A binding ended (08 §7.3) and what it held was removed, restored or released.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `name` (string): The name it was given, or empty.
- `what` (string): `trait`, `entity`, `edit`, `area` or `rule`.
- `why` (string): `duration`, `dismissed`, `dispelled`, `mode`, `suppressed`, `dormant`, `owner_stops`, `revoked`, `lost`, `moved` or `owner_removed`.
- `how` (string): What was done: `remove`, `restore` or `release`.
- `thing` (any): What it held: the entity, the area, the one a trait or rule was on, or the first conjured cell.

<a id="body-changed"></a>
## `body_changed`

A body was edited (06 §6.5): its functions, channel slots, mass and attributes have been worked out again, and the events of what changed raised.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `verb` (string): Which edit: `add_part`, `remove_part`, `replace_part`, `graft_part`, `set_layer`, `scale_part`, `scale_body`, `set_body_plan` or `damage_part`.
- `part` (string): The name of the part edited, or of the part a new one went on; empty for an edit of the whole body.
- `parts` (int): How many parts the body has now that are there.

<a id="body-destroyed"></a>
## `body_destroyed`

A body is in pieces: its root part was destroyed (06 §7.5). Whether that ends the creature is decided by its definitions (06 §8.3).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="body-hit-occupant"></a>
## `body_hit_occupant`

A body in flight struck an entity, `target`, in the cell `here` (02 §15.2). The world has shared their momentum and changed nothing else: what the blow does is for the simulation. A body that is an entity is the event's `actor`.

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `body` (int): The body's id.
- `owner` (string): What the body is: `entity`, `debris` or `projectile`.
- `tag` (int?): For a projectile, the number it was launched with; otherwise null.
- `energy` (real): The joules of the blow: the whole energy of the body's motion.
- `intensity` (real): How concentrated the blow was, in pascals.

<a id="body-impact"></a>
## `body_impact`

A body in flight struck a floor, block or fixture; `here` is the element's cell (02 §15.2). What the blow did to the element is reported by the element's own events. `target` is the entity the body is, if it is one: what the blow does to it is for the simulation.

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `body` (int): The body's id.
- `owner` (string): What the body is: `entity`, `debris` or `projectile`.
- `tag` (int?): For a projectile, the number it was launched with; otherwise null.
- `layer` (string): `floor`, `block` or `fixture`.
- `energy` (real): The joules of its motion the body lost.
- `intensity` (real): How concentrated the blow was, in pascals.
- `result` (string): What the blow did to the element: `unaffected`, `damaged` or `destroyed`.

<a id="body-landed"></a>
## `body_landed`

A body has come to rest and is a body no longer (02 §15.3). A fragment has been left as rubble. An entity, `target`, is in the cell `here`, back in the simulation's hands.

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `body` (int): The body's id.
- `owner` (string): What the body is: `entity`, `debris` or `projectile`.
- `tag` (int?): For a projectile, the number it was launched with; otherwise null.

<a id="body-launched"></a>
## `body_launched`

Something has been set flying: from now on the world moves it (02 §15). `target` is the entity the body is, if it is one; `here` is the cell it starts in.

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `body` (int): The body's id.
- `owner` (string): What the body is: `entity`, `debris` or `projectile`.
- `tag` (int?): For a projectile, the number it was launched with; otherwise null.
- `mass` (real): Its mass in kilograms.
- `speed` (real): How fast it starts, in m/s.

<a id="body-left-loaded"></a>
## `body_left_loaded`

A body's flight has taken it out of loaded space and has been finished by arithmetic; `here` is the last loaded cell it was in (02 §15.4). If it does not return it is a body no longer: its impact waits with the tract it came down in.

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `body` (int): The body's id.
- `owner` (string): What the body is: `entity`, `debris` or `projectile`.
- `tag` (int?): For a projectile, the number it was launched with; otherwise null.
- `returns` (bool): Whether it comes back into loaded space and flies on as a body.
- `energy` (real): The joules of its motion as it arrives.

<a id="cell-var-changed"></a>
## `cell_var_changed`

A variable on a cell was set, changed or cleared.

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `key` (string): The variable's qualified name.
- `old` (any): Its value before; null if it had none.
- `new` (any): Its value after; null if it has none.

<a id="checkpoint-made"></a>
## `checkpoint_made`

A rule asked for a checkpoint (13 §9.1). The application saves it at the next safe point, unless the game's saving policy is `none`.

Subjects: none of its own.

Fields:

- `name` (string): The checkpoint's name.

<a id="choice-made"></a>
## `choice_made`

A choice put by a rule's `ask` was answered (05 §10.6): by the `Choose` command, or at once for an entity that is not directly controlled. The option's effects run next.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `choice` (int): The number of the choice.
- `option` (int): The position of the option taken, from zero.
- `label` (string): Its label, as it was shown.

<a id="clock-rate-changed"></a>
## `clock_rate_changed`

The rate of an entity's personal clock, an area's clock or a realm's clock changed, or a clock was given or taken away (03 §3.4).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `area` (area).

Fields:

- `clock` (int): The clock's id.
- `old` (real?): Its rate relative to its parent before; null if there was no such clock.
- `new` (real?): Its rate after; null if the clock is gone.

<a id="collapse-settled"></a>
## `collapse_settled`

A collapse has ended: nothing of it is in flight and no check is waiting near it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `collapse` (int): The collapse's id.

<a id="collapse-started"></a>
## `collapse_started`

A stability check found something giving way where no collapse was in progress. `here` is the cell whose change started it (02 §14.3).

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `collapse` (int): The collapse's id.

<a id="contents-materialised"></a>
## `contents_materialised`

A container's latent contents were made (06 §9.3): it was opened, searched or hit for the first time.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `count` (int): How many entities were made.

<a id="control-changed"></a>
## `control_changed`

Who decides for an entity changed (03 §5.1).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `old` (string): The mode before: `none`, `direct` or `delegated`.
- `new` (string): The mode after.

<a id="cutscene-cued"></a>
## `cutscene_cued`

An action that names a cutscene began (07 §10, 12 §8.1), once its `requires_at_start` held: a cue for the application to show it. `self` started it; `other` is the participant of its second role, for a joint action. What happens is the simulation's to decide, as for any action.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `other` (entity).

Fields:

- `cutscene` (string): The cutscene the action names (12 §8.1), as written.
- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action that began.
- `id` (int): The number of the running action.
- `participants` (list<entity>): Everyone taking part, in the order of the roles: whoever started it first.

<a id="decal-added"></a>
## `decal_added`

A mark was left in a cell.

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="decals-removed"></a>
## `decals_removed`

Every mark of one kind was removed from a cell.

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `count` (int): How many marks there were.

<a id="decision-needed"></a>
## `decision_needed`

An entity that is not directly controlled is free to act and has nothing planned (03 §5.2). Whatever decides for it answers by starting an action or a wait; if nothing does, it idles and is asked again.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `control` (string): Who decides for it: `none` or `delegated`.
- `why` (string): Why it is free: `started`, `finished`, `interrupted`, `plan_empty` or `waited`.

<a id="decision-requested"></a>
## `decision_requested`

A directly controlled entity must choose. Time does not move until it has.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `kind` (any): What is being asked (03 §5.2).

<a id="detected"></a>
## `detected`

`self`'s awareness of `about` through a sense reached 1: it knows what and where, and its track is brought up to date (15 §5.1).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `about` (entity).

Fields:

- `sense` (string): The qualified id of the sense.
- `where` (loc?): Where it was perceived.

<a id="device-configured"></a>
## `device_configured`

A setting of a device was set (16 §4.2) by `set_config`. The value is kept with the device and saved with it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `key` (string): The setting's id.
- `old` (any): What it held before.
- `new` (any): What it holds now.

<a id="device-demoted"></a>
## `device_demoted`

A device entity was dropped: its element is back in its default state with nothing inside it, or the element is gone. When it is delivered the device no longer exists; `element` is what it was bound to.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `element` (element).

No fields.

<a id="device-mode-changed"></a>
## `device_mode_changed`

A device's mode changed (16 §4.2): by `set_mode`, from a rule, an interaction or a machine's own rules. Recipes under way at it work at the speed the new mode gives from now on.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `old` (string): The mode it was in.
- `new` (string): The mode it is in now.

<a id="device-promoted"></a>
## `device_promoted`

An element became a device entity bound to it (02 §5.5): its state left the default, something was put inside it, or a rule asked. `self` is the device, `element` what it gives behaviour to.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `element` (element).

No fields.

<a id="device-spilled"></a>
## `device_spilled`

Something came out of a device whose element was destroyed or replaced (02 §5.5): an item lies in the cell, someone who hid there stands in it. `here` is where it came to rest.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `device` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `layer` (string): Which of the cell's elements the device was bound to: `floor`, `block` or `fixture`.

<a id="disguise-seen-through"></a>
## `disguise_seen_through`

An observer saw through what an entity presents (15 §8.2): it takes it for its true persona, and where the persona shown is one the entity made, it has linked the two in its own beliefs, and in nobody else's.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `about` (entity).

Fields:

- `shown` (string): The persona `about` presents, as text (`7v1/2`).
- `seen` (string): The persona the observer now takes it for: its true one.
- `how` (string): `checked`, by `identity_check`, or `revealed`, by `reveal_persona`.

<a id="dosed"></a>
## `dosed`

A body took a substance in by a route (16 §9.5): once for each substance of a dose, after its pools and traits.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `substance` (string): The substance's qualified id.
- `amount` (real): What got in, in millilitres: its volume times the route's factor.
- `route` (string): `ingest`, `inject`, `skin` or `breath`.

<a id="driver-changed"></a>
## `driver_changed`

Who acts for `self`'s body changed: `driver` is who does now, and is not bound when nobody does (06 §8.2).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `driver` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="element-changed"></a>
## `element_changed`

A floor, block or fixture was set, replaced, transmuted or removed.

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `layer` (string): `floor`, `block` or `fixture`.

<a id="element-damaged"></a>
## `element_damaged`

The accumulated damage of an element changed.

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `layer` (string): `floor`, `block` or `fixture`.
- `old` (int): Damage before, in 255ths of the element's capacity.
- `new` (int): Damage after.

<a id="element-destroyed"></a>
## `element_destroyed`

A floor, block or fixture was destroyed: by damage, by the load on it, or by falling (02 §12.3).

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `layer` (string): `floor`, `block` or `fixture`.
- `how` (string): `damage`, `crushed` or `fell`.
- `absorbed` (real): The joules it took from the packet that destroyed it.
- `passed` (real): The joules of that packet that carried on beyond it.

<a id="energy-released"></a>
## `energy_released`

A release has gone as far as it goes; `here` is where it was let go (02 §13). It sums what the release did: rules that keep account of what someone has broken listen to this, not to every element.

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `release` (int): The release's id.
- `energy` (real): How much was let go, in joules.
- `absorbed` (real): The joules that elements took from it. Never more than was let go.
- `reach` (real): How far its front got, in metres.
- `cells` (int): How many cells its front visited.
- `cut_off` (bool): Whether it was cut off before its reach for the budget of cells.
- `elements` (int): How many elements it destroyed.
- `mass` (real): The mass of what it destroyed, in kilograms.
- `exposed` (int): How many times an entity was exposed to it.
- `thrown` (int): How many entities it threw.

<a id="entity-created"></a>
## `entity_created`

An entity came to exist. It is not yet anywhere: `entity_relocated` follows when it is put somewhere.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="entity-demoted"></a>
## `entity_demoted`

A hot character became warm (09 §9.2): ranked beyond `sim.max_hot_minds`. It no longer sweeps, hears only loud things and is stepped in bulk; what it was doing runs on.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="entity-died"></a>
## `entity_died`

An entity's mind stopped driving it for good (06 §8.3). It is still there, with its body, its wounds and what it holds. Control of it was released first.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="entity-exposed"></a>
## `entity_exposed`

Something struck the cell an entity is in: a mass that landed there (02 §14.3). The entity receives the packet the cell did. Follows the world's `occupant_exposed`.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `kind` (string): The kind of damage: the qualified id of a `damage_type`.
- `energy` (real): Joules delivered to the cell.
- `intensity` (real): How concentrated the delivery was, in pascals.

<a id="entity-promoted"></a>
## `entity_promoted`

A character stepped warm became hot (09 §9.2): its senses sweep again and its mind thinks at once, going on with what it was doing.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `why` (string): Why: `attention` (ranked under the cap at a warm step), `seen` (the party came to see it), `involved` (an action that started names it) or `acting` (its own mind was to start an action).

<a id="entity-relocated"></a>
## `entity_relocated`

An entity's place changed: it moved, was put inside something or taken out, entered the world or left it. What it holds moves with it and is not reported.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `from` (any): Where it was: a cell and a height, a container, or not in the world.
- `to` (any): Where it is. `here` is bound when that is a cell.

<a id="entity-removed"></a>
## `entity_removed`

An entity ceased to exist. What it held was put where it was first.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="entity-revived"></a>
## `entity_revived`

A dead entity's mind drives it again (06 §8.3).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="entity-spawned"></a>
## `entity_spawned`

An entity was made from templates and is complete (06 §10.3).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `templates` (list<string>): The qualified ids of the templates it was made from, in the order applied.
- `items` (list<string>): What it is to start with, as its templates and chosen options wrote it: for whoever makes items.
- `traits` (list<string>): The traits it is to start with, as written: for whoever gives traits.

<a id="entity-unconscious"></a>
## `entity_unconscious`

An entity's mind stopped driving it for now: something its definitions say it cannot do without is gone (06 §8.3).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="entity-unsupported"></a>
## `entity_unsupported`

What held an entity up has gone: its floor, the solid top below it or the stairs it stood on (02 §14.3). It is where it was. Follows the world's `occupant_unsupported`.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="entity-woke"></a>
## `entity_woke`

An unconscious entity's mind drives it again.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="event-cancelled"></a>
## `event_cancelled`

A hook was cancelled: what it preceded did not happen. The hook's own subjects are not bound; its cause is carried.

Subjects: none of its own.

Fields:

- `event` (string): The name of the hook that was cancelled.
- `code` (string): The stable code of the reason.
- `message` (string): Why, as the handler that cancelled it said.

<a id="fault"></a>
## `fault`

The engine contained a fault: a limit was exceeded, or something was scheduled that nothing handles. Not delivered to handlers; it goes straight to the output.

Subjects: none of its own.

Fields:

- `code` (string): The stable code of the reason.
- `message` (string): What went wrong, in a sentence.

<a id="fell"></a>
## `fell`

An entity had nothing under it where it could not stay and began to fall from `here`: the world carries it as a body from now on. `landed` follows when it comes to rest.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="field-appeared"></a>
## `field_appeared`

A field came to be in a cell that held none of it (02 §16). Other changes of a field's level are not reported. Which field it is cannot be tested by a filter.

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `level` (int): The level it has there, 1 to 255.

<a id="field-budget-exceeded"></a>
## `field_budget_exceeded`

There are more active field cells than the budget allows: until there are fewer, the weakest decay faster. Reported when a step first finds it so; `here` is the first cell of that step (02 §16).

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `active` (int): How many field cells are active.
- `max` (int): The most there may be.

<a id="field-contact"></a>
## `field_contact`

A field and an entity came to share a cell: the field appeared where the entity is, or the entity moved to where the field is. Reported once, not at every step (02 §16).

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `level` (int): The level the field has there.

<a id="field-vanished"></a>
## `field_vanished`

The last of a field left a cell (02 §16).

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="function-changed"></a>
## `function_changed`

What the body can do of something changed: a part that provides it was damaged, healed, disabled, restored or lost.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `function` (id<body_function>): The function.
- `old` (real): Its capacity before.
- `new` (real): Its capacity now.

<a id="goal-adopted"></a>
## `goal_adopted`

`self`'s mind took up a goal (09 §3.3): it scored best by more than the held goal's `commit`, or a rule set it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `goal` (string): The qualified id of the goal taken up.
- `about` (any): What it is about: an entity, a memory as a map, a cell, or null.
- `score` (real): Its score when it was taken up.
- `previous` (string?): The qualified id of the goal it displaced, if any.

<a id="goal-done"></a>
## `goal_done`

The goal `self`'s mind held is done: its `done` held (09 §3.2).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `goal` (string): The qualified id of the goal.

<a id="goal-failed"></a>
## `goal_failed`

The goal `self`'s mind held failed: its `fail` held, or no method of it could be used. It is set aside for its `retry_after` (09 §4).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `goal` (string): The qualified id of the goal.
- `code` (string): The stable code of the reason.
- `message` (string): Why, in words.

<a id="grip-broken"></a>
## `grip_broken`

A grip of `self` on `target` ended (07 §9.1), and what it pinned works again.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part?): The part that was held.
- `how` (string): `ended`: its action ended; `released`: the holder let go; `broken`: the held broke free; `thrown`: the held was thrown; `lost`: they came apart.

<a id="group-created"></a>
## `group_created`

A group was made in play by `create_group` (15 §9.2).

Subjects: none of its own.

Fields:

- `group` (string): The group's key (15 §9.2).
- `def` (string): The group definition's qualified id.

<a id="group-dissolved"></a>
## `group_dissolved`

A group was dissolved by `dissolve_group` (15 §9.2): its members have left it.

Subjects: none of its own.

Fields:

- `group` (string): The group's key (15 §9.2).

<a id="group-joined"></a>
## `group_joined`

An entity joined a group (15 §9.2), and was told what the group knows.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `group` (string): The group's key (15 §9.2).
- `role` (any): Its role, or null.

<a id="group-left"></a>
## `group_left`

An entity left a group, or the group was dissolved (15 §9.2).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `group` (string): The group's key (15 §9.2).
- `role` (any): The role it had, or null.

<a id="hit-exited"></a>
## `hit_exited`

Energy of a hit left the far side of a body (06 §7.2). With a direction, the block of the next cell along it has already been struck with it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `part` (part?): The part it left through; null if the hit met no part.
- `kind` (id<damage_type>): The kind of damage.
- `energy` (real): Joules that left the far side.
- `intensity` (real): How concentrated they are, in pascals.
- `dir` (list<real>?): The direction they travel in: east, south and up.

<a id="hit-landed"></a>
## `hit_landed`

A hit did something to a part. Raised once for each part reached, outermost first: the part struck, then a part inside it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part): The part struck.
- `kind` (id<damage_type>): The kind of damage.
- `absorbed` (real): Joules the part's own layers took.
- `passed` (real): Joules that went on through them.
- `depth` (int): How many of the part's layers the hit got through.

<a id="interacted"></a>
## `interacted`

An interaction was done: its effects have run (16 §3.4).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity), `element` (element).

Fields:

- `interaction` (string): The qualified id of the interaction.

<a id="item-broken"></a>
## `item_broken`

An item's damage reached all 255 parts. It is still there: it adds no layer when worn, and what else being broken means is a rule's to say.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="item-damaged"></a>
## `item_damaged`

An item's damage rose, by a packet or by what it absorbed as a worn layer.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `old` (int): Its damage before, in 255ths.
- `new` (int): Its damage now.
- `kind` (string): The kind of damage: the qualified id of a `damage_type`.

<a id="item-dropped"></a>
## `item_dropped`

A thing left whatever held it and lies where its holder was: in the holder's cell, or inside whatever encloses the holder. The cause says who or what made it happen.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `holder` (entity).

Fields:

- `count` (int): How many members the entity has.

<a id="item-merged"></a>
## `item_merged`

Equal items joined into one stack. `self` is the stack that remains; the entity that joined it is gone.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `count` (int): How many members joined.

<a id="item-removed"></a>
## `item_removed`

A worn item came off `holder`. `item_taken` or `item_dropped` follows, saying where it went.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `holder` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="item-repaired"></a>
## `item_repaired`

An item's damage fell.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `old` (int): Its damage before, in 255ths.
- `new` (int): Its damage now.

<a id="item-split"></a>
## `item_split`

Members of a stack were split off as an entity of their own, in the same place and hold.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `piece` (entity).

Fields:

- `count` (int): How many members the piece has.

<a id="item-taken"></a>
## `item_taken`

A thing entered a hold other than a worn one: it was taken into a grasp, stowed, or put inside. `from` is what held it before, if anything did.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `holder` (entity), `from` (entity).

Fields:

- `hold` (string): The kind of hold: `grasp`, `worn`, `stowed`, `seat`, `inside` or `fixed`.
- `count` (int): How many members the entity has.

<a id="item-worn"></a>
## `item_worn`

An item was put on: it now covers parts of `holder` and is a layer for hits on them.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `holder` (entity).

Fields:

- `parts` (int): How many parts it covers.

<a id="know-how-gained"></a>
## `know_how_gained`

A mind came to know something (16 §8.5).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `know_how` (string): The know-how's qualified id.
- `how` (string): `template`, `taught` or `read`, or what the rule that taught it said.

<a id="know-how-lost"></a>
## `know_how_lost`

A mind no longer knows something (16 §8.5 `unlearn`).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `know_how` (string): The know-how's qualified id.
- `how` (string): `unlearned`.

<a id="landed"></a>
## `landed`

The world has stopped carrying an entity as a body: it came to rest at `here`, after a fall or after being thrown. What the landing does to it is for whoever turns impacts into hits (06 §7); the blows themselves are the world's `body_impact`.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `height` (real): How far below where it set off it came to rest, in metres; zero if it came to rest higher.
- `speed` (real): How fast something falling that far lands, in metres a second: `sqrt(2 g h)`, with nothing taken off for the air.
- `energy` (real): The energy of a fall that far, in joules: its mass, with what it carries, times gravity times the height.

<a id="launched"></a>
## `launched`

A push launched `self` as a body in flight (02 §15), or added to the velocity of one already in flight. The world carries it until it lands (`landed`).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `speed` (real): Its speed, in metres a second.
- `dir` (list<real>): Its direction: east, south, up.
- `added` (bool): True if it was already in flight and the push was added to its velocity (07 §7.1).

<a id="lost-track"></a>
## `lost_track`

`self`'s awareness of something it had detected fell to 0 through a sense: it no longer perceives it there (15 §5.1).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `about` (entity).

Fields:

- `sense` (string): The qualified id of the sense.
- `where` (loc?): The last known place: where the track ends.

<a id="memory-added"></a>
## `memory_added`

`self` remembered something (15 §7.1).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `event` (string): What is remembered: an event type or any name.
- `where` (loc?): Where it happened.
- `salience` (real): How much it matters, 0 to 1.

<a id="memory-forgotten"></a>
## `memory_forgotten`

`self` forgot its least salient memory to make room for another (15 §7.1).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `event` (string): What was forgotten.
- `where` (loc?): Where it happened.

<a id="message"></a>
## `message`

A rule's `message` (05 §10.6): a line for the log of whoever controls `self`.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `text` (string): The line, rendered for `self` as its reader.
- `style` (string): How it is to be shown: a style name of the interface, or empty.

<a id="message-heard"></a>
## `message_heard`

A message was heard and understood (15 §11). `speaker` is bound if the hearer made out who spoke; `about` and `to` if the message named them. A report's beliefs have been gained, and an order received, before this is delivered.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `speaker` (entity), `about` (entity), `to` (entity).

Fields:

- `kind` (string): The message kind's qualified id.
- `text` (any): The line it was said with, written for the hearer as reader, or null.
- `addressed` (bool): Whether it was said to the hearer: to it, to a group it belongs to, or to nobody in particular.
- `report` (bool): Whether the hearer gained beliefs from it: a report said to it that carried something.
- `clarity` (real): How far over its sense's threshold it was heard.
- `where` (loc): Where it seemed to come from: the speaker's cell when it was said.

<a id="method-chosen"></a>
## `method_chosen`

`self`'s mind began to follow a method of its goal (09 §17). Raised only while something listens for it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `goal` (string): The qualified id of the goal.
- `method` (int): The method's position in the goal's `methods`.

<a id="mind-released"></a>
## `mind_released`

Raised at death, after `entity_died`: the hook for whatever collects minds (06 §8.3).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

No fields.

<a id="mind-transferred"></a>
## `mind_transferred`

The mind that was in `self` is now in `target`, with what is seated in it (06 §8.2).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity).

Fields:

- `swap` (bool): Whether the two minds changed places.

<a id="mission-done"></a>
## `mission_done`

Every objective of a mission is done. Its `on_done` has run.

Subjects, in delivery order: `taker` (entity).

Fields:

- `mission` (string): The mission definition's qualified id.
- `serial` (int): The mission's number in this game, from 1.

<a id="mission-expired"></a>
## `mission_expired`

A mission's `expires` ran out while it was active. Its `on_expired` has run.

Subjects, in delivery order: `taker` (entity).

Fields:

- `mission` (string): The mission definition's qualified id.
- `serial` (int): The mission's number in this game, from 1.

<a id="mission-failed"></a>
## `mission_failed`

An objective of a mission failed, its `failed` came to hold, or `fail_mission` was called. Its `on_failed` has run.

Subjects, in delivery order: `taker` (entity).

Fields:

- `mission` (string): The mission definition's qualified id.
- `serial` (int): The mission's number in this game, from 1.

<a id="mission-started"></a>
## `mission_started`

A mission was started (13 §5.2): its objectives that wait for nothing are shown.

Subjects, in delivery order: `taker` (entity).

Fields:

- `mission` (string): The mission definition's qualified id.
- `serial` (int): The mission's number in this game, from 1.

<a id="mode-ended"></a>
## `mode_ended`

A mode ended (08 §5.4): its trait and its upkeep are gone together, and its `on_end` has run.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `mode` (string): The mode's id within the ability.
- `how` (string): `ended` (switched off), `empty` (its upkeep ran a pool dry), `dormant`, `suppressed`, `revoked`, `lost`, `rank` (the rank fell below it) or `moved` (with a mind to another body).

<a id="mode-started"></a>
## `mode_started`

A mode was switched on (08 §5.4): its trait is given and its upkeep runs.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `mode` (string): The mode's id within the ability.

<a id="objective-changed"></a>
## `objective_changed`

An objective was shown, done or failed (13 §5.1). Its `on_done` or `on_failed` has run. `taker` is who it is for.

Subjects, in delivery order: `taker` (entity).

Fields:

- `id` (string): The objective's id.
- `state` (string): What it is now: `active` (shown), `done` or `failed`.
- `mission` (int): The number of the mission it is part of; 0 for one of the scenario's own.

<a id="occupant-displaced"></a>
## `occupant_displaced`

An edit left an entity no room and it was moved to the nearest cell with room. `entity_relocated` follows.

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="occupant-dosed"></a>
## `occupant_dosed`

An entity stands in a field whose `expose` rule adds to a pool. Reported once for each step of the field, for the strongest cell of it the entity fills. The world applies no route and no guard: what reaches the pool is for the simulation (02 §16).

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `level` (int): The level the field has there.
- `pool` (string): The pool the field's `expose` rule adds to, as its definition writes it.
- `amount` (real): The dose: the level times the rule's `per_level`.
- `route` (string): The route the dose takes: `breath`, `skin` or `any`.

<a id="occupant-entombed"></a>
## `occupant_entombed`

An edit left an entity no room and there was nowhere near to go. It stays where it is.

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="occupant-exposed"></a>
## `occupant_exposed`

Something struck the cell an entity is in. `entity_exposed` follows.

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `energy` (real): Joules delivered to the cell.
- `intensity` (real): How concentrated the delivery was, in pascals.

<a id="occupant-unsupported"></a>
## `occupant_unsupported`

What held an entity up has gone. `entity_unsupported` follows.

Subjects, in delivery order: `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="option-chosen"></a>
## `option_chosen`

A `choose` step of `self`'s mind started an action (09 §17). Raised only while something listens for it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `purpose` (string): The purpose the `choose` step named.
- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action started.

<a id="order-cancelled"></a>
## `order_cancelled`

An order an entity kept no longer stands (15 §10).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `order` (int): The order's number.
- `how` (string): `cancelled` by `cancel_order`, `expired` past its `until`, or `relation_lost` when the relation that made it one to obey fell to its default.

<a id="order-given"></a>
## `order_given`

An order was heard and kept by the one it was given to (15 §10): it stands until cancelled, until its time is up, or until the relation that made it one to obey is lost. What is done about it is a goal's, or a rule's (the bundled `core:do_as_ordered`).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `giver` (entity).

Fields:

- `order` (int): The order's number, for `cancel_order`.
- `action` (any): The action the order says to do: an id of an `action`.
- `with` (any): The action's parameters, by name.
- `until` (any): When it stops standing, in seconds of universal time from now, or null for good.

<a id="order-refused"></a>
## `order_refused`

An order heard by the one it was given to was not obeyed (15 §10): it holds no relation flagged `orders` toward the giver, did not make the giver out, or a handler of `order_received` refused.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `giver` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (any): The action the order says to do: an id of an `action`.
- `reason` (string): The code of why: `social.not_obeyed`, `social.giver_unknown`, or a handler's.
- `message` (string): Why, in words.

<a id="part-destroyed"></a>
## `part_destroyed`

A part was destroyed: every layer of it is gone. What was on it came off with it. For the root, the body is in pieces.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part): The part.

<a id="part-detached"></a>
## `part_detached`

A part came off a body with everything on it and in it: cut off or destroyed by a hit, or taken off by an edit (06 §7.5). `self` is whose body it was and `here` is where that body stands. In Rust the event carries the part itself, for whoever makes an item of it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `part` (string): The name, in the body it came off, of the part that came off.
- `how` (string): `severed`, `destroyed` or `removed`.
- `mass` (real): The mass of the part and everything that went with it, in kilograms.
- `parts` (int): How many parts came off: the part and what was on it and in it.
- `leaves_item` (bool): Whether the part's definition says it leaves an item, and not nothing.

<a id="part-disabled"></a>
## `part_disabled`

A part stopped working: its condition fell below its `disable_below`, or something disabled it. It contributes nothing and its channel slots are gone.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part): The part.

<a id="part-restored"></a>
## `part_restored`

A part works again: its condition is back, or what disabled it let go.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part): The part.

<a id="part-severed"></a>
## `part_severed`

A part came off, with everything on it and in it. Raised for the part cut, not for what went with it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part): The part.
- `parent` (part?): The part it was joined to.

<a id="party-gone"></a>
## `party_gone`

No directly controlled character of the party remains alive (13 §9.3). `self` is the last of them. Raised once, before what follows is done.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `then` (string): What follows, by the scenario's `on_party_gone`: `end`, `continue` or `restore`.

<a id="path-failed"></a>
## `path_failed`

No path could be planned for a mover to a cell, bound as `here`. Whatever path it was following is forgotten.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `code` (string): The code of the reason (06 §11).
- `message` (string): The reason, as a sentence.

<a id="perceived"></a>
## `perceived`

`self` perceived something (15 §6). `about` is who or what it appeared to be about, if the observer made that out: until personas, the entity, which a mind may read only through its belief properties. Its cause names no actor.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `about` (entity).

Fields:

- `percept` (string): `detection`: awareness of `about` reached 1; `signal`: a signal that was given off was received.
- `sense` (string): The qualified id of the sense.
- `signal` (string): The qualified id of the kind of signal that carried it.
- `event` (string?): The type of the event the signal carried, if it carried one.
- `about_actor` (entity?): Whom the observer took the event's actor for: someone it had detected, or seen where the signal came from. Null if it made out nobody. The true actor is not given.
- `where` (loc?): Where it seemed to come from.
- `clarity` (real): How far over the threshold it was received: received over threshold.

<a id="phase-entered"></a>
## `phase_entered`

A phase of an action began. The event's own stamp is the start; `duration` and `due` are the scheduled end (03 §12).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `id` (int): The number of the running action, which no other action of this simulation ever has.
- `phase` (string): The id of the phase.
- `held` (bool): Whether the phase lasts until it is let go.
- `duration` (real?): How long it will last, in seconds of the actor's own clock; null for a held phase with no `max`.
- `due` (int?): The universal tick it is due to end at as the clocks now run, in microseconds; null where there is no duration or the clock is stopped.

<a id="phase-exited"></a>
## `phase_exited`

A phase of an action ended normally: its `on_exit` has run.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `id` (int): The number of the running action, which no other action of this simulation ever has.
- `phase` (string): The id of the phase.

<a id="plan-cleared"></a>
## `plan_cleared`

An entity's plan was emptied: by `ClearPlan`, by `clear_plan` or `interrupt_plan`, or because a step's `requires` failed when it came due (03 §5.3).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `code` (string?): The code of the reason, if a step could not be started or a rule interrupted the plan.
- `message` (string?): That reason, in a sentence.

<a id="pool-crossed"></a>
## `pool_crossed`

A pool's level crossed one of its thresholds, by a rate, a verb or a change of its `max`. Raised once for each threshold crossed, in the order they were crossed.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `pool` (id<pool>): The pool.
- `threshold` (real): The threshold crossed, as the fraction of `max` the definition lists.
- `rising` (bool): True if the level rose to the threshold or past it; false if it fell to it or below.
- `level` (real): The pool's level after the crossing.

<a id="posture-changed"></a>
## `posture_changed`

An entity's posture changed, and with it its height (06 §11.1).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `from` (string): The qualified id of the posture it was in; empty for none.
- `to` (string): The qualified id of the posture it is in; empty for none.
- `look` (string): The `look` of the posture it is in, as its definition writes it; empty for none.

<a id="poured"></a>
## `poured`

Something was poured out of a container (16 §9.5): into another, or onto a cell. `self` is what it came out of.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `amount` (real): The volume that left it, in cubic metres.
- `onto` (any): Where it went: the container, or the cell.

<a id="projectile-fired"></a>
## `projectile_fired`

`self` fired a projectile (07 §11.1), aimed at `target` if at anyone, with `weapon` if with anything. Raised once for each projectile, before any of it strikes. Content gives it off as a sound and a light (15 §3.2), so that shots are heard and seen.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity), `weapon` (entity).

Fields:

- `projectile` (string): The qualified id of the projectile; empty for an item thrown.
- `body` (int?): The number of its body in flight (02 §15); null for an instant shot.
- `speed` (real): Its speed as it left, in metres a second.
- `energy` (real): The energy it left with, in joules.
- `noise` (real): How loud the shot was: the weapon's `shot.noise`, or the effect's.
- `flash` (real): How bright the shot was: the weapon's `shot.flash`, or the effect's.
- `instant` (bool): Whether it was cast as a ray and struck at once (07 §11.3).

<a id="projectile-hit"></a>
## `projectile_hit`

A projectile, or an item thrown, fired by `self` struck `target`, or the element of the cell `here` (07 §11.1). What the hit did is told by the body's, the item's or the world's own events.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `projectile` (string): The qualified id of the projectile; empty for an item thrown.
- `body` (int?): The number of its body in flight (02 §15); null for an instant shot.
- `part` (part?): The part of `target` it landed on; null for an element or an item.
- `energy` (real): Joules it arrived with.
- `intensity` (real): How concentrated, in pascals: the energy over its surface's area times its give.
- `absorbed` (real): Joules what it struck took: the target's layers and what it wears, an item, an element.
- `passed` (real): Joules it went on with beyond what it struck.
- `instant` (bool): Whether it was an instant shot.

<a id="projectile-passed"></a>
## `projectile_passed`

A projectile, or an item thrown, fired by `shooter` passed within `projectile.near_miss` of `self` without striking it (07 §11.1). Told once for each projectile. What being shot at does to a person is content.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `shooter` (entity).

Fields:

- `projectile` (string): The qualified id of the projectile; empty for an item thrown.
- `body` (int?): The number of its body in flight (02 §15); null for an instant shot.
- `distance` (real): How close it passed to the middle of `self`, in metres; zero for one that went by at a height where nothing of `self` was.

<a id="rank-changed"></a>
## `rank_changed`

An ability's rank changed (08 §4.1): its track advanced, or `set_rank` set it. What applies from a rank (`at_rank`) has been brought into line.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `ability` (string): The qualified id of the ability.
- `old` (int): The rank before.
- `new` (int): The rank now.

<a id="recipe-completed"></a>
## `recipe_completed`

A recipe's work is done (16 §8.2): its outputs are made, what it mends is mended and its `result` has run, unless it was spoiled.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `station` (entity).

Fields:

- `recipe` (string): The recipe's qualified id.
- `spoiled` (bool): Whether it came to nothing.

<a id="recipe-stalled"></a>
## `recipe_stalled`

A recipe under way stopped advancing (16 §8.2): its worker stopped, its station does not work in its mode, a store it draws on ran dry, its condition on the place does not hold, or its worker's rate came to nothing. Its work done is kept.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `station` (entity).

Fields:

- `recipe` (string): The recipe's qualified id.
- `why` (string): `stopped`, `station`, `supply`, `condition` or `worker`.

<a id="recipe-started"></a>
## `recipe_started`

A recipe began, its inputs used up, or resumed where it was left (16 §8.2).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `station` (entity).

Fields:

- `recipe` (string): The recipe's qualified id.
- `resumed` (bool): Whether it goes on with work already done.
- `work` (real): How much work it takes in all, in seconds at a rate of 1.

<a id="relation-changed"></a>
## `relation_changed`

A relation a mind holds of its own changed (15 §9.1): set, added to or cleared. Fading is not a change: it is worked out when the relation is read.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `kind` (string): The relation kind's qualified id.
- `toward` (string): Whom it is held toward: a persona as text, or a group's key.
- `group` (bool): Whether `toward` is a group.
- `value` (real): The value now.
- `was` (real): The value before: the kind's default if it was not held.

<a id="release-started"></a>
## `release_started`

Energy has been let go at a point: its front starts to spread from `here` now (02 §13).

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `release` (int): The release's id.
- `energy` (real): How much was let go, in joules.
- `reach` (real): How far it will reach with nothing in its way, in metres.

<a id="role-changed"></a>
## `role_changed`

A member's role in a group changed by `set_role` (15 §9.2).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `group` (string): The group's key (15 §9.2).
- `role` (any): Its role now, or null.
- `was` (any): Its role before, or null.

<a id="route-blocked"></a>
## `route_blocked`

A change in the world blocked the path `self` was following at `here`: the path is planned again before its next step (09 §5.2).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc).

No fields.

<a id="said"></a>
## `said`

`self` said something (a `say` step, 09 §4). Content gives it a signal with an `event_signal`, so that others hear it. Speech (15 §11) will raise its own.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `text` (string): What was said.
- `volume` (real): How loud, as a factor content gives its signal; 1 for an ordinary voice.

<a id="scenario-ended"></a>
## `scenario_ended`

The game ended (13 §9.4). The application shows the summary and applies the saving policy.

Subjects: none of its own.

Fields:

- `as` (string): The outcome the ending names.
- `reason` (string): Why, where an ending stands in for something refused (a `restore` with no checkpoint); else empty.

<a id="scenario-started"></a>
## `scenario_started`

A game began (13 §12): the party is placed, its settings and rules are in force and `start.do` has run. `self` is the first of the party.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `scenario` (string): The scenario's qualified id.
- `place` (int): Which of its places the party began at, from 0.

<a id="seized"></a>
## `seized`

`self` took hold of `target` (07 §9.1). The grip lasts as long as the action that took it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part?): The part held; null for none in particular.
- `pins` (bool): Whether it pins that part.
- `action` (int): The number of the holder's action that maintains it.

<a id="setting-changed"></a>
## `setting_changed`

The `Setting` command, or a scenario as it began, changed a setting (04 §10).

Subjects: none of its own.

Fields:

- `key` (string): The setting's key.
- `old` (any): What it was; null if it was not set.
- `new` (any): What it is now.

<a id="slots-gained"></a>
## `slots_gained`

Channel slots are back with a part that works again (06 §6.4).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part): The part that supplies them.
- `channels` (list<id<channel>>): The channels, in order of channel.
- `counts` (list<int>): How many slots of each, in the same order.

<a id="slots-lost"></a>
## `slots_lost`

Channel slots are gone with a part that stopped working or came off (06 §6.4). An action that held one of them is to be interrupted (03 §6.2).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part): The part that supplied them.
- `channels` (list<id<channel>>): The channels, in order of channel.
- `counts` (list<int>): How many slots of each, in the same order.

<a id="spawn-requested"></a>
## `spawn_requested`

A tract that has just been loaded asks for something to be put into the world at `here`: its generator's request, or one left for it (02 §9.4).

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `what` (string): What to make: the id of a definition, as the request wrote it.
- `realm` (int): The realm's id.

<a id="staggered"></a>
## `staggered`

A push staggered `self` (07 §7): too slow to move it, fast enough to unbalance it. What staggering does is content.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `speed` (real): The speed the push would give it, in metres a second.
- `severity` (real): Where that speed lies between `combat.stagger_at` and `combat.launch_at`, from 0 to 1.
- `dir` (list<real>): The direction of the push: east, south, up.

<a id="step-failed"></a>
## `step_failed`

A step of the method `self`'s mind was following failed: its action was refused or interrupted, or it could not find its target (09 §4). The method is given up and the next is tried.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `goal` (string): The qualified id of the goal.
- `step` (string?): The kind of step: `go`, `do`, …
- `code` (string): The stable code of the reason.
- `message` (string): Why, in words.

<a id="step-refused"></a>
## `step_refused`

A step, or a placement by `move_to`, was refused when it was tried: the mover is where it was.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `dir` (string): The direction of the step: `north` to `north_west`, `up` or `down`; empty for a placement.
- `code` (string): The code of the reason (06 §11).
- `message` (string): The reason, as a sentence.

<a id="step-started"></a>
## `step_started`

`self`'s mind began a step (09 §17). Raised only while something listens for it.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `goal` (string): The qualified id of the goal.
- `step` (string): The kind of step.

<a id="strike-defended"></a>
## `strike_defended`

A strike by `self` at `target` met a defence of `defender` in force that covered it (07 §5, step 5 of 07 §3.4). Raised once for each defence tried, in the order they are tried.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity), `defender` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action whose attack it is.
- `attack` (string): The id of the attack within it.
- `defence` (string): The qualified id of the defending action.
- `form` (string): `avoid` or `interpose`.
- `succeeded` (bool): Whether it succeeded. An `avoid` that succeeded makes the strike miss (`strike_missed` with `why` `defence`).
- `margin` (real?): The margin of the defence's contest; null for one with none.
- `turned` (real): Joules it turned aside (07 §5.3); zero for one that avoids or failed.

<a id="strike-landed"></a>
## `strike_landed`

A strike by `self` landed on `target`, or on the element of the cell `here` (07 §3.4, step 8). What the hit did to the body is told by the body's own events (06 §7.6).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity), `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action whose attack it is.
- `attack` (string): The id of the attack within it.
- `part` (part?): The part it landed on; null where the body chose one, or for an element.
- `kind` (id<damage_type>): The kind of damage it delivered.
- `energy` (real): Joules it delivered as harm: its energy at the effort given, less the push.
- `intensity` (real): How concentrated that was, in pascals: the energy over the surface's area times its give (07 §6.1).
- `absorbed` (real): Joules the target's layers and what it wears took, or the element took.
- `passed` (real): Joules that went on beyond it.
- `returned` (real): Joules that came back into the surface that struck (07 §6.3).
- `push` (real): Joules set aside to push the target (07 §7).
- `effort` (real): The effort it was made with, 0 to 1.
- `margin` (real?): The margin of its aim; null for a strike that did not aim.

<a id="strike-missed"></a>
## `strike_missed`

A strike by `self` missed `target` (07 §3.4, steps 2 and 4).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action whose attack it is.
- `attack` (string): The id of the attack within it.
- `why` (string): `reach`: the target was not within reach; `aim`: the margin of aim was too low; `nothing`: the target has no body and is not an item.
- `margin` (real?): The margin of its aim, where it aimed.

<a id="strike-recoiled"></a>
## `strike_recoiled`

Energy a strike by `self` delivered that the target neither absorbed nor passed came back into the surface that struck: the part of `self`, or the item `weapon` (07 §6.3). Whatever it did is told by the body's or the item's own events. Not raised for an inline surface, which takes nothing.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `weapon` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action whose attack it is.
- `attack` (string): The id of the attack within it.
- `part` (part?): The part of `self` whose surface struck and took it back; null for an item or an inline surface.
- `energy` (real): Joules that came back into the surface (07 §6.3).
- `absorbed` (real): Joules of it the part's layers or the item took.

<a id="strike-stopped"></a>
## `strike_stopped`

A strike by `self` reached `target` and nothing of it was delivered: a handler of `hit_incoming` cancelled the hit (06 §7.6).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `target` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action whose attack it is.
- `attack` (string): The id of the attack within it.
- `code` (string): The code of the reason nothing was delivered.
- `message` (string): The reason, as a sentence.

<a id="suspicion-raised"></a>
## `suspicion_raised`

`self`'s awareness of `about` through a sense crossed that sense's `suspect`: something is there (15 §5.1).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `about` (entity).

Fields:

- `sense` (string): The qualified id of the sense.
- `level` (real): The awareness now, 0 to 1.

<a id="tag-changed"></a>
## `tag_changed`

An entity was given a tag it did not have, or lost one it had (`add_tag`, `remove_tag`).

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `tag` (string): The tag.
- `added` (bool): Whether it was added; false if it was taken away.

<a id="tasted"></a>
## `tasted`

Something swallowed tasted of something (16 §9.5): the substance with the strongest `taste` in what was taken in by `ingest`, for rules to notice.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `substance` (string): The substance's qualified id.
- `taste` (real): How strongly, from 0 to 1.

<a id="thrown"></a>
## `thrown`

`self` threw the item `what` (07 §11.1), aimed at `target` if at anyone. It flies as a body (02 §15) and strikes with the surface it was thrown with.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `what` (entity), `target` (entity).

Fields:

- `speed` (real): Its speed as it left the hand, in metres a second.
- `energy` (real): The energy it left with, in joules.

<a id="ticket-refused"></a>
## `ticket_refused`

A ticket was refused because the tickets together wanted more tracts than may be loaded. It is no longer held (02 §10.3).

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `realm` (int): The realm's id.
- `ticket` (int): The id the ticket had.

<a id="track-advanced"></a>
## `track_advanced`

A track reached a level. Raised once for each level, lowest first, when one advance passes several.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `track` (id<track>): The track.
- `level` (int): The level reached.

<a id="tract-loaded"></a>
## `tract_loaded`

A tract has been loaded. `here` is its cell with the lowest horizontal coordinates, at storey 0. The entities that were waiting for it are put back (02 §9.4).

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `realm` (int): The realm's id.
- `first` (bool): Whether the tract has never been loaded before.

<a id="tract-unloading"></a>
## `tract_unloading`

A tract is about to be unloaded. The entities standing in it leave the world and wait for it to be loaded again (02 §9.5).

Subjects, in delivery order: `here` (loc).

Fields:

- `realm` (int): The realm's id.

<a id="trait-added"></a>
## `trait_added`

An entity was given a trait (06 §5): it gained it, or one it had from the same giver was refreshed or gained a stack. What it confers is applied before this is raised.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `trait` (string): The qualified id of the trait.
- `giver` (string): What gave it: `rule`, `item`, `posture`, `ability`, `template` or `other`.
- `stacks` (int): How many stacks the instance has now: 1 unless it stacks.
- `first` (bool): Whether the entity did not have the trait from this giver before: false for a refresh or another stack.
- `duration` (real): How long it will last, in seconds of the holder's time; null for one that lasts until removed.
- `look` (string): The trait's `look` as its definition writes it (12 §4.4); empty for none.

<a id="trait-expired"></a>
## `trait_expired`

A trait's duration ran out (03 §9). `trait_removed` follows, with `how` `expired`.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `trait` (string): The qualified id of the trait.
- `giver` (string): What gave it: `rule`, `item`, `posture`, `ability`, `template` or `other`.

<a id="trait-removed"></a>
## `trait_removed`

A trait, or some of its stacks, is gone (06 §5), and what it conferred with them has been taken back. The trait's own attached rules are detached before this is delivered: a trait answers its own ending with `on_remove`.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `trait` (string): The qualified id of the trait.
- `giver` (string): What gave it: `rule`, `item`, `posture`, `ability`, `template` or `other`.
- `stacks` (int): How many stacks went.
- `left` (int): How many stacks of the instance are left: 0 when it is gone.
- `how` (string): `removed` by `remove_trait`, `expired`, `replaced` by a trait of the same group, or `withdrawn` by what gave it: an item let go, a posture left.
- `look` (string): The trait's `look` as its definition writes it (12 §4.4); empty for none.

<a id="var-changed"></a>
## `var_changed`

A variable declared with `"watch": true` changed (05 §6). What it lives on is bound under the name of its kind: an entity as `self`, a cell as `here`, an area, a site, a tract or a realm under those names; a global variable binds nothing.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `here` (loc), `area` (area), `site` (site), `tract` (tract), `realm` (realm).

Fields:

- `name` (string): The variable's qualified name.
- `scope` (string): The kind of what the variable lives on: `entity`, `loc`, `area`, `site`, `tract`, `realm` or `global`.
- `old` (any): What it read as before: its value, or its default if it was not set.
- `new` (any): What it reads as now.

<a id="window-closed"></a>
## `window_closed`

A window closed (03 §7.1): the phase that is its deadline began, its action ended, or its length was over. `self` is whose action or rule opened it. A candidate still waiting to notice it never does.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `window` (window): The window: what `react` and `ask_reaction` are given.
- `kind` (string): The qualified id of its kind.
- `action` (string?): The qualified id of the action whose phase opened it; null for a window no action opened.
- `offered` (int): How many candidates it was offered to.
- `noticed` (int): How many of them noticed it in time.
- `reacted` (int): How many answered it with a reaction.

<a id="window-noticed"></a>
## `window_noticed`

`self` noticed a window opened by `source` before it closed (03 §7.2). A rule may answer with `react` or `ask_reaction`; with nothing listening, nothing happens.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity), `source` (entity).

Fields:

- `window` (window): The window: what `react` and `ask_reaction` are given.
- `kind` (string): The qualified id of its kind.
- `action` (string?): The qualified id of the action whose phase opened it; null for a window no action opened.
- `named` (bool): Whether the window names `self`: false for one offered for someone else.
- `time_left` (real?): Seconds of `self`'s own time before the window is expected to close; null where that is not known.

<a id="window-opened"></a>
## `window_opened`

A phase that opens a reaction window began (03 §7.1). Its candidates are worked out next and start to notice it (03 §7.2); the window itself reaches rules through `window_noticed`.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `action` (string): The qualified id of the action's definition.
- `id` (int): The number of the running action, which no other action of this simulation ever has.
- `kind` (string): The qualified id of the window's kind.
- `closes` (string): The id of the phase whose start closes it.
- `count` (int): How many it is aimed at.

<a id="wound-closed"></a>
## `wound_closed`

A wound stopped leaking: its time came, or `close_wound` closed it. What it goes through begins to heal.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `wound` (wound): The wound.
- `part` (part): The part it is on.

<a id="wound-healed"></a>
## `wound_healed`

A wound is gone: every layer it went through is whole again.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `part` (part): The part it was on.
- `kind` (id<damage_type>): The kind of damage it was.

<a id="wound-inflicted"></a>
## `wound_inflicted`

A hit breached a part, or made a wound of the same kind that was open there worse. For a part that came off, the wound is the stump, on the part it was joined to.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `wound` (wound): The wound.
- `part` (part): The part it is on.
- `kind` (id<damage_type>): The kind of damage.
- `depth` (int): How many layers it goes through.
- `area` (real): Its area, in square metres.

<a id="wound-reopened"></a>
## `wound_reopened`

A closed wound was opened again by `reopen_wound`: it leaks as it did.

Subjects, in delivery order: `self` (entity).

Fields:

- `wound` (wound): The wound.
- `part` (part): The part it is on.
